correctness.rationale: For prime powers p^m, m=p^{m-2} gives only p,m=(3,3),(2,4). For odd two-prime support, parity makes one exponent even, one odd; the b=1 branch yields a quadratic discriminant product of size 8A and impossible bounds, while b>=3 forces q^2|A and p^2|(2B+1), contradicting exponential>linear. For support {2,p} parity forces odd-prime exponent even, and p^2|k, yielding 2^{p^2 C-1}p^{2B-2}=2C+B, impossible by elementary bounds. All exponent boundaries checked.
